title: How to Build Your Own AI Data Center in 2025 — Paul Gilbert, Arista Networks
talk_summary: This is a data-center networking talk about GPU cluster fabrics (spine/leaf, RoCEv2, PFC/ECN, buffer tuning, telemetry), not about agent orchestration or LLM application design. The transferable ideas are mostly about isolating expensive shared resources, matching resource allocation to actual traffic/packet patterns, and instrumenting failures with rich diagnostics rather than dropping them silently.

takeaways.technique: Isolate the expensive compute fabric from general workloads
takeaways.what_they_do: They build the GPU backend network completely isolated from storage/frontend and internet, with nothing else attached, because the GPUs are expensive and bursty.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when people build AI networks in the Enterprise uh we don't connect nothing else to the these networks

takeaways.technique: Tune buffers to the actual packet/workload size
takeaways.what_they_do: They observe that models send a particular packet size and tune switch buffers exactly to that, since buffering is expensive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: models send and receive a particular size packet and what we do is we adjust those buffers to accept those types of packets

takeaways.technique: Capture diagnostics on failure instead of silent drops
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of dropping congested packets silently, they snapshot the packet and headers and report why it was dropped, plus GPU-side agents report stats to correlate GPU vs network faults.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we'll drop the packet but we'll actually take a snapshot of the packet and the headers any rme information in it and we'll tell you why we dropped it

takeaways.what_they_do: They instrument the network so ops knows about degradation before the developer call comes in, using telemetry and visibility.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you always want to be aware of the problem before you get the call from the developers

takeaways.technique: One slow worker stalls the whole synchronized job
takeaways.what_they_do: Because GPUs are synchronized, a single slow GPU becomes a barrier that stops everyone; they treat job completion time as the key metric.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have a slow GPU that's a barrier because it stops everyone else job completion time is what matters
